raw:
{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status", "description": "Admitting struggle feels like losing the reputation they have worked hard to build as a high performer." },
  "read": "They have tied their sense of who they are to being the person who handles everything without complaint. Saying 'I need help' feels like a threat to that identity, not just an admission of being tired. The 'I'm fine' is protective armor, not dishonesty.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Back off, stop raising it, and quietly redistribute their work without telling them, which signals you think they cannot handle the truth and robs them of any say in their own situation." },
  "mentorMove": "Hold the standard that sustainable performance is non-negotiable on your team, while opening a real conversation that lets them define what adjustments would actually help, so they stay in the driver's seat of the solution.",
  "holdFirm": ["Burnout is a performance and retention issue, not a personal preference, so the workload conversation is happening regardless of their self-assessment.", "You are not asking for their permission to care about their sustainability, only for their input on how to address it."],
  "stayFlexible": ["They get to name which projects are draining versus energizing, so any rebalancing reflects their priorities.", "The timeline and method for redistributing load can flex around what protects their reputation with the rest of the team."],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I want to carve out fifteen minutes with you, no agenda document, just a real check-in. I am bringing this up because you are one of the most reliable people I have, and that is exactly why I am paying attention." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "When I look at your calendar and your output over the last couple of months, I see someone carrying a heavy load. I am not asking you to tell me you are struggling. I am asking you to help me understand what the volume actually feels like from the inside right now. What does a normal Tuesday look like for you these days?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I want to figure out together: which parts of your current load are genuinely yours to own versus stuff that landed on you because you are the person who never says no. I want us to map that out, because there is likely at least one thing we can move or share without touching the work that actually matters to you." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I have high standards for this role, and I also have a standard for how people on this team are able to work over the long run. I am holding you to both, because I know you are capable of delivering at a high level without running yourself into the ground. What I need from you is one honest answer: if you could change one thing about your current workload this week, what would it be?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "Over the next few weeks, check in briefly and consistently, not to monitor them but to normalize the idea that flagging capacity is a sign of professional self-awareness, not weakness. The goal is to reshape their identity story slightly, from 'I am the person who never needs anything' to 'I am the person who performs at a high level sustainably,' which is actually a more durable and senior professional identity."
}
situation: One of my best people is clearly overworked and heading for burnout but insists they are fine.
